fix(installer): use User-scope PATH in Windows install instruction (#1072) (#1274)

The printed PATH instruction used $env:PATH, which is the merged
Machine+User PATH. Writing it back to User scope copies all Machine
entries into User scope, corrupting the User PATH and pushing it
toward the 8191-char limit.

Changed to read User scope separately before modifying:
  $userPath = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('PATH', 'User')
  [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('PATH', "...;$userPath",

fix(install): aceitar SHA256SUMS em modo binário no instalador (#605)

O install.sh extraía a linha do artefato com grep de dois espaços
("<hash>  <nome>", modo texto GNU). O SHA256SUMS publicado no v0.2.1
usa modo binário ("<hash> *<nome>", um espaço + asterisco), então o

The Server-Sent Events (SSE) handler connected its Redis subscriber with no

vanished client on an idle zombie was only ever detected on the next write —

fix(cto): bound RESP parse recursion depth (P2)

readRespValue recursed once per array element with no depth bound, so a
malformed or hostile REdis Serialization Protocol (RESP) reply of the form
`*1\r\n*1\r\n…` would recurse until the worker thread's stack overflowed — an
unrecoverable crash, not a catchable error. The replies we actually consume
(XREADGROUP / XAUTOCLAIM) nest ~5 levels.

Thread a depth counter through a private readRespValueDepth and reject past
MAX_RESP_DEPTH (16) with error.
